title: Maximal chains of primes in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring have length the dimension
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension $d=\dim S$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] (finite, as $S$ is Noetherian local), and assume that $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(S)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak m$ contains an $S$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $d$. Let $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ be a maximal chain of prime ideals of $S$, that is, a chain of prime ideals that cannot be lengthened by inserting a prime ideal before $\mathfrak p_0$, between two consecutive members, or after $\mathfrak p_n$ (so $\mathfrak p_0$ is a minimal prime ideal of $S$, $\mathfrak p_n=\mathfrak m$, and no prime ideal lies strictly between $\mathfrak p_{i-1}$ and $\mathfrak p_i$). Then $n=d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00N9 (lemma-maximal-chain-CM, line 25345: 'Let R be Noetherian local. Suppose R is Cohen-Macaulay of dimension d. Any maximal chain of ideals p_0 ⊂ p_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ p_n has length n = d'), proved there as a special case of lemma-maximal-chain-maximal-CM (line 25151); Cohen-Macaulay local ring as in definition-local-ring-CM (line 25308)
